title: Many Young People Following Health Influencers
paragraphs: Many young people are now getting information about their health from influencers on social media, according to new data from the Pew Research Center in the US.

In July 2026, Pew published new findings from surveys of more than 5,000 American adults that were carried out in 2025. Overall, about 40% of all US adults said they get health or wellness information from social media influencers or podcasts. However, the number was much higher among young people.

Among people aged 18 to 29, 57% of women and 47% of men said they get health information from influencers. In comparison, among people aged 50 and older, only 29% of women and 25% of men said the same.

Young men and women also hear about different topics. For example, 51% of young women often hear about beauty and appearance from influencers, compared with only 18% of young men. Young women were also about twice as likely to hear about treatments outside of mainstream medicine. On the other hand, young men were more likely to hear about fitness.

Why do young people use influencers? The most common reason was that they wanted to change their health or lifestyle. About 51% of young women and 37% of young men said this was a major reason. Some young people also said they use influencers to learn about things that they do not want to ask their doctor about.
Still, according to Pew, doctors and other health care providers are the most common source of health information for Americans.
A separate survey by the research company EMARKETER found that 83% of Gen Z and millennials who look for health information online follow or interact with health influencers.
